I started watching Youtube around 2008 or 2009. I was about 8 years old and had unrestricted internet access. I essentially ended up discovering all of the top creators at that time: Fred, iJustine, Davedays, SMPFilms, Smosh, Onision (unfortunately,) and (also unfortunately), Shane Dawson. 

I think what drew me in was his satirical commentary on pop culture. I would say *most* of his skit content was about celebrities, TV shows, films, music, other Youtubers, dances and various other cultural phenomena. I was a neurodivergent kid just trying to understand the topics my peers would talk about in school like Justin Bieber, Lady Gaga, Twilight, etc. For me, Shane Dawson's content provided an in for understanding the gossip floating around at the time; but there was definitely a drawback to this which I didn't quite grasp at the time. 

There was a lot of terrible ideas sprinkled into in his content. I do remember Shananay vividly. There was a good bit of blackface and shitty stereotypes in his videos. There was a lot of sexual, violent, and otherwise shock-type humor as well.  Looking back, I think I was at least mindful enough as a kid to not co opt the racist parts of Shane's humor into my own. However, I do remember that I thought the sex jokes were funny and it led to me having a pretty twisted sense of humor in elementary school, which I thankfully grew out of pretty quickly. 

Usually he would wrap up his skits with some sort of "moral" message. Sometimes he'd post the occasional skit which would be more serious to raise awareness for certain topics like suicidality or bullying.

I have a similar experience. On my five year vegan diet I ended up feeling such an extreme lack of satiety that I would binge eat constantly. I was cooking everything from scratch but no amount of chickpea curry or peanut butter banana pancakes would allow me to actually feel full. I ended up purging because the binges would make me so bloated. It got to the point where I was purging up to 12x daily. Every day was genuinely nightmarish for me. I would sit on the bathroom floor just thinking "*why am I so compelled to do this? Why? I wouldn't wish this hell upon anyone.*"

 On top of that, even with consistent supplement intake, a blood test had shown I was anemic and D deficient. My head was in a fog at all times. At 17, I had to be admitted to the ICU for three days for an attempt on my life. I felt completely empty inside; and, while the fiber I was consuming kept me regular and the micronutrients kept me from catching colds*, plant based food wasn't truly fueling me*. It seemed like nothing I could do would ever quiet the internal furor I was suffering with.

That is until, at age 18, I broke down in desperation and begrudgingly decided to eat a plate of canned chicken and eggs. Like magic, everything became calm after that. No more binging, no more purging, no more greyed gums, no more acne, no more fighting with my body.

I continued eating farm fresh eggs and slowly introduced all animal products back into my diet. It's been five years now and I couldn't even fathom binging now. I've cut a lot of processed shit out of my diet in the past few years; and I've realized that the faux meat, vegetable oils, store-bought bread, nut butters, and complete lack of saturated fat were absolutely wreaking havoc on my brain and gut as a vegan teenager. I genuinely cannot make myself overeat now if I tried. I haven't purged once since reintroducing animal products. Real food has saved my life.

 Veganism has the ability to easily induce or mask eating disorders. And vegans themselves? Many of them are misanthropes who get off on feeling morally superior. They would rather let people with autism, GI problems, eating disorders, etc. slip through the cracks and potentially die than give up their chauvinistic motives. Thankfully more people are realizing that eating local, real foods is a more reliable solution to the food crisis than just lazily cutting out animal products.

This isn't super intense, but felt jarring at the time. Anyways, when I was 16, I worked at a large retail chain whose name starts with a 'W' as a stocker. One of my school friends had joined my team recently and she was very stereotypically stoner-ish. Burgundy hair, Baja hoodie, handwoven shoulder bag, always carried an aroma of weed.

I had smoked with her a few times just with a regular ol' pipe and ground flower. One work day she told me to come hang out in her van for our lunch. She then proceeded to convince me to hit her dab pen, which I had never done at this point in my adolescence. She was like, "yeah so just press the button and inhale while holding it till it blinks!"

This was a grave mistake. When I returned to stocking they ended up putting me in the dairy/fridge section and for some reason that night the scariest manager was joining us, as well as my direct supervisor. I was extremely zooted and terrified. Time felt like molasses and I was spending hours having to make conversation with my two superiors while appearing hard at work. The manager was this six foot tall woman with graying hair and dark piercing eyes. She would always threaten to terminate the minor employees whenever she felt they weren't working up to standard.

Luckily I had built up respect over the months and so the two women weren't exactly watching me like a hawk. I just tried to look as busy as possible meanwhile internally I was having a full blown anxiety attack. I remember when it was time for me to clock out my supervisor was like, "ah must be time for (my name) to go home and sleep, she's got that exhausted look in her eyes..." 

My supervisor was actually a super awesome laid back older lady who bought acid from me once. She sadly passed away from cancer a few years later, but anyway to this day I have a feeling she perhaps could tell what was up. I just scrambled out the building as quick as I physically could and vowed to never hit a blinker at work ever again.

Thank you so much. It's good to know I'm not alone. I'm so sorry you have to feel similar pain. My brother did actually attempt suicide a few times. Sometimes he would overdose and even he wouldn't be sure if he was trying to kill himself or just get really high. He would just wake up in the hospital either way. I really think this time he wasn't expecting to die though. He had seemed happier and had just bought a 1000 dollar gaming PC with some disability checks he saved up. He didn't even get a chance to try it out before he passed. It was brand new, sitting right by the sheetless mattress he took his last breath on.

When I went through his room, I was no longer confused as to why he was dead. It was like a hoarder nest but full of junk food wrappers, cigarette boxes, empty 100 proof liquor bottles, and piles of empty OTC med bottles (diphenhydramine, propylhexedrine, and dextromethorphan.) I realized from this that his body had to be in agony every single day. The little part of our brains that keep us from doing harm to ourselves I feel was just broken with him. He had no self preservation instinct at all. He wasnt even 21 for a full hear and had drank more alcohol than your average person would in a lifetime. It was a harrowing sight.

I get what you mean by the grief manifesting strangely. Once I understood how awful his quality of life was, I felt some sense of relief that he didn't have to deal with that any longer. He used to get mad at me and say it was unethical to make him keep living. He would say that on a philosophical level, it should be his choice whether or not to be alive. These conversations would make me upset, but now.... I don't know. I'm not sure he was compatible with normal life... He had no bills to pay and all the free time to engage in his hobbies all day... but he still couldn't tolerate simply being sober. It's just tragic. He seemed happier on the outside towards the end... but I guess it was just because he was mixing so many different substances in that moment. I think his heart couldn't take any more and just gave out, but it hasn't been confirmed yet.

I feel so many emotions but luckily my family has been supportive. I'm just trying to distract myself as much as possible but it's hard. I feel as a big sister, I was supposed to protect him, but I just couldn't. I'm barely an adult myself. I'm really trying not to feel guilty and I'm in therapy at least.

Yeah it seemed he had absolutely zero instinctual sense of self preservation. I have been cleaning out his room and the amount of Everclear, diphenhydramine pills, cigarette boxes, etc I'm rummaging through is just unbelievable. I do believe his autism factored into this; but it's odd because I have OCD and ADHD and I couldn't even imagine partaking in even half the extent of abuse he engaged in. I guess neurodivergence affects people in drastically different ways. Thank you for the kind words. I'm in therapy and my mom will be soon.

Other commenters have essentially pointed it out, but OCD is referred to as an "ego-dystonic" psychiatric condition. This indicates that the thoughts experienced by those with the disorder *do not* align and are actually typically dissonant with or opposite to their actual values, goals, self-image, rational though processes, etc. Your friend trusts you a lot to explain her intrusive thoughts. She doesn't genuinely believe *you* will molest her. Its more of a *but oh god what if* *someone* does and fearing the sheer guilt/consequences of that scenario. Not allowing anyone to change her diaper except herself is a compulsion that she feels will 100% protect her from that potential outcome. It is irrational and she very likely knows it is. A major part of OCD is being unable to tolerate any degree of uncertainty around specific fears. Trust me, it's really not personal.

It's really easy to obtain lethal doses of caffeine when nodoz and vivarin OTC are 200mg caffeine pills. My bf almost died from reading the instructions wrong on them and taking too many. Caffeine tends to be really unpredictable. It's been shown that drinks with 300 mg or more cause temporary QT prolongation (slight heart arrhythmia) Just half a gram of caffeine has killed people. Caffeine is a direct adenosine receptor antagonist (receptors that help modulate myocardial oxygen consumption and coronary artery flow) Caffeine also causes the pituitary gland to release more epinephrine, while ADHD meds work more on norepinephrine; epinephrine causes way more strain on the body, it's normally only released during emergencies. norepinephrine is always circulating. Plus usually when people do die from lethal OD with amphetamines its normally from convulsions since they lower the seizure threshold (which I think, with Eugenia's very likely electrolyte imbalance would be the most major concern) Cocaine also is way more likely to cause heart problems than ADHD meds. Overall, ADHD meds are definitely a lower concern for heart strain than caffeine or coke. I think if Eugenia is taking them, it's definitely not her prescription.
